## Context / Problem

CI runs the suite with `-n 3 --dist worksteal`, and the `lru_cache` on
`_rendered()` in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py:60`
is process-local, so each xdist worker that lands one of its four consumers
re-renders all 178 corpus bodies (~884 pandoc spawns). Measured on this
worktree (macOS, pandoc 3.6.1 via `pypandoc-binary==1.15`):

* serial (`-p no:randomly`, no xdist): ONE test pays the fill —
  `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` 47.92s, the other three
  consumers ~0s. 135.09s wall, 38.10s user + 48.69s system.
* `-n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300`: THREE tests each pay a full fill —
  44.49s, 43.38s, 42.82s. 92.03s wall but 63.96s user + 79.50s system.

So the filed premise holds: three cache fills under `-n 3` versus one serially,
about +56s of CPU burned re-deriving an identical, immutable artifact. On a
3-core macOS runner three concurrent 884-spawn pandoc storms also contend with
the rest of the suite, which is what produced the 321.6s/495.6s aggregates cited
on the parent audit.

A second duplication shows in the same runs: the three
`test_dc_corpus_passes_two_to_five_are_byte_identical[...]` tests each recompute
`first = render_markdown_to_wiki(body)` per body — bit-for-bit the pass-1 render
`_rendered()` already holds. They cost 23.85s/25.93s/22.34s serially, about half
of which is that recomputed pass 1.

## Approach

Replace the process-local `lru_cache` with a **session-scoped artifact shared
across xdist workers on disk**, and have the fixed-point tests read pass 1 from
it instead of recomputing it.

* A session-scoped fixture `corpus_pass1` resolves the shared directory as
  `tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent`. Under xdist a worker's basetemp is
  `pytest-<N>/popen-gw<K>`, so `.parent` is `pytest-<N>` — shared by every worker
  of THIS session and rotated by pytest between sessions: cross-worker sharing
  with no new dependency and no artifact that outlives the session.
* The artifact is **sharded per stratum** (one file per `code_arrow`/`table`/`prose`),
  and each worker probes the strata in an order rotated by its
  `PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER` index. That is a scheduling hint only — the lock still
  guarantees one computation per stratum — but it stops concurrent whole-corpus
  consumers from queueing on the same shard, so a cold session costs one stratum of
  wall time instead of the whole corpus.
* The artifact filename embeds a SHA-256 digest of the three corpus JSON files,
  the `wiki_render` module source, and the resolved pandoc executable path +
  size, so a corpus or renderer edit can never be served a stale render.
* Mutual exclusion uses `os.mkdir` on a sibling lock directory (atomic on POSIX
  and Windows, no new dependency): the winner renders, publishes via `os.replace`
  (atomic, so a visible artifact is always complete), and removes the lock in a
  `finally` block, retiring it on the success AND the error path. A loser that
  sees neither lock nor artifact re-enters the acquisition loop. **The loser's
  fallback deadline is 150s** — below the `--timeout=300` guard, with headroom
  over the fill — so a loser blocked on a crashed winner breaks the orphaned lock,
  renders locally, and still finishes inside the timeout instead of being killed
  by it: it degrades to today's per-worker behaviour rather than deadlocking.
* The four `_rendered()` consumers and the three fixed-point tests all take the
  fixture. The fixed-point tests keep their own pass-2 (and conditional pass-3)
  renders — that is real, non-duplicated coverage.

This fits because the render is a pure function of the inputs the digest pins, so
sharing it weakens no assertion, and it targets the duplication directly rather
than cutting corpus coverage, which the parent audit and the coordinating tickets
refused. Caching pass 1 (not pass 2) keeps the largest test far below the hang
guard instead of concentrating the whole corpus into one test.

## Scope

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py` — replace the
  `lru_cache`d `_rendered()` (line 60) with the digest-keyed cross-worker
  artifact plus a session fixture; convert the four consumers
  (`test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained`,
  `test_dc_corpus_tables_survive_verbatim`,
  `test_dc_corpus_html_comments_survive_exactly`,
  `test_dc_corpus_coverage_ratios`) and the three
  `test_dc_corpus_passes_two_to_five_are_byte_identical` parametrizations to the
  fixture; update the module docstring's cost-discipline note.

No production file changes: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py`
is read (for its source bytes in the digest and via its existing public
`render_markdown_to_wiki`/`code_fragments`) but not modified. Corpus fixtures
under `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/` are unchanged.

## Testing

The changed unit is itself the test module, so verification is by running it and
comparing against the recorded baselines above:

* Happy path — `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py
  -n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300 --durations=12`: all 11 tests still pass,
  and exactly one test shows a fill-sized duration while the other `_rendered()`
  consumers drop to well under a second.
* Serial path — the same module with no xdist still passes, proving the shared
  artifact degrades correctly when there is a single worker.
* Failure/edge path — a temporary local corpus mutation is confirmed to change the
  digest, forcing a fresh render instead of serving the previous artifact; and a
  temporary renderer defect that drops a protected code fragment is confirmed to
  still fail `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` through the cached
  path. Both mutations are reverted; neither is committed.
* Whole-suite regression — the CI pytest command is green.

No wall-clock or timing-budget assertion is added to any test; the savings are
recorded as ticket-comment evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] All 178 corpus bodies and every existing assertion (cardinality, secret
      scrub, protected excerpts, tables, HTML comments, determinism, fixed point,
      coverage ratios, non-vacuity) still run against real pandoc — verified by
      `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_wiki_render_corpus.py` reporting
      11 passed with no test skipped or deleted.
- [x] Under the exact `-n 3 --dist worksteal --timeout=300` command, each
      stratum's pass-1 render is computed exactly once per session: no worker shows
      a whole-corpus (>30s) fill, versus the three 42-45s fills measured today —
      recorded as a before/after ticket comment.
- [x] Aggregate per-test time for the module under that command is at least 40%
      below the 211s baseline recorded above, measured by summing `--durations=12`
      setup+call times and posted as a ticket comment.
- [x] Total CPU (user+system) for that command is below the 143s baseline recorded
      above, posted as a ticket comment.
- [x] No single test in the module exceeds 120s under `-n 3`, keeping clear of the
      300s hang guard — read off the same `--durations` output.
- [x] `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` and
      `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/*.json` are byte-identical to `origin/main`,
      confirmed by `git diff --stat origin/main -- <those paths>` being empty.
- [x] A locally seeded corpus edit is shown to change the artifact digest and
      force a fresh render rather than serve the previous artifact — evidence in a
      ticket comment, mutation reverted.
- [x] A locally seeded protected-fragment break is shown to still fail
      `test_dc_corpus_protected_excerpts_are_retained` through the cached path —
      evidence in a ticket comment, mutation reverted.
- [x] The loser fallback deadline in the committed code is below the
      `--timeout=300` guard, confirmed by reading the constant in the diff.
